sections.html:
Hoffman Estates is a village in the northwest suburbs, mostly in Cook County with a very small part in Kane County. Mail is delivered under ZIP codes 60169, 60010 and 60192. Population was 52,530 in the 2020 census and is estimated at 50,858 in mid-2025.

Sam and Jack Hoffman, a father and son who ran a construction company, bought 160 acres in 1954 and began building homes. The village incorporated on September 23, 1959. The count rose from 8,296 in 1960 to 46,363 in 1990, so many houses are several decades old, and a buyer will ask how old the roof, furnace and windows are.

The 2020 to 2024 survey counts 18,537 households. Of the homes, 74.2 percent are owned, with a median value of $351,900. Renters pay a median gross rent of $1,734. Just over a quarter of homes have renters, so investor-owned and tenant-occupied houses come up in sales. About 46.4 percent of residents age 5 and older use a non-English language at home, so translated showing instructions and listing documents can help.

The Prairie Stone Business Park, a 750-acre planned district bounded by Illinois Route 59, Interstate 90, Illinois Route 72 and Beverly Road, anchors employment in the village. It took shape after Sears relocated its headquarters there in 1993. St. Alexius Medical Center is the largest local employer at 2,500 workers. Commutes average 28.5 minutes, and Woodfield Mall in neighboring Schaumburg is close by.

A transfer or job change can force a quick sale, and proximity to this much employment is a fair point to make in a listing.

Several districts overlap here, so the assigned school follows the street address.

  • North of Interstate 90, Township High School District 211 serves high school students.
  • In that northern area, Community Consolidated School District 15 (K to 8) serves addresses east of Huntington Boulevard.
  • Barrington School District 220 (K to 12) serves addresses west of Huntington Boulevard in the same area.
  • Residents west of Barrington Road primarily attend Elgin Area U46.

Most of the village is in Harper College Community College District 512. Confirm the district for your exact address before you name any school in a listing.

The Village's transfer tax dates to 1987 and falls on the seller of any real estate sold or transferred inside Village limits. Payment and the stamp come before closing and recording, and the Village prints the cost as $3 per $1,000 of the selling price.

  • Allow 48 hours of notice so staff can process the stamp, and send applications or questions to transferstamps@vohe.org.
  • Bring the state transfer declaration (PTAX-203/EZ Dec) and the deed or other document going to the recorder.
  • Call the Water Department at 847-843-4824 at least five days before buying the stamp to order a final water bill.
  • Call 847-882-9100 or use that same email to confirm no liens or fines remain on the property and the garbage bill is paid.
  • An exempt stamp costs a $10.00 administrative fee, needs the fully executed deed carrying the exempt language and signature, and calls for a final water reading if ownership changes.

Stamps are sold at the Village Hall front counter at 1900 Hassell Road on weekdays during business hours, or by mail with a self-addressed stamped return envelope. Settle with your closing agent who will buy the stamp and on what day.

Most of the village sits in Cook County, so deeds go to the Cook County Clerk's recordings division at 118 N. Clark Street. A deed costs $107, which bundles the county recording fee, a GIS fee, a document storage fee, the State Rental Housing Support Fee and a non-government filer fee. Mail-in recording with return adds $5 per document.

The seller is liable for two more charges: .50 per $500.00 for the State of Illinois and .25 per $500.00 for Cook County. The statute behind the state tax is 35 ILCS 200/31-10.

sections.h2: Order of tasks from contract to closing
sections.html:
Count backward from closing day, because each step waits on the one before it.

  1. Call the Water Department first and request the final water bill, at least five days before you plan to buy the stamp.
  2. Confirm with the Village that no liens or fines remain and that the garbage bill is paid.
  3. Give the Village 48 hours of notice, then buy the stamp with the PTAX-203/EZ Dec and the deed in hand.
  4. Record the deed with the Cook County Clerk, or with the Kane County recorder if your parcel is in the small Kane portion.

Placing the water call first avoids the likeliest delay. Ask the title company which county rates apply to your parcel.

Most delays come from paperwork nobody collected until the week of closing. Pull these together once you have a signed contract, or earlier if you can.

  • The deed or whichever document is going to the recorder, with the exempt language and signature if the transfer is exempt.
  • The state transfer declaration, PTAX-203/EZ Dec.
  • Your latest water and garbage bills, so staff can confirm nothing is unpaid.
  • Any permit paperwork for work done on the house, since a buyer's inspector may ask about a finished basement, a new roof or replaced windows.

Stamp questions go to 847-882-9100, and the stamp email address is transferstamps@vohe.org. If you live out of the area, ask about the mail-in option so you do not need to stand at the front counter on a weekday. Keep a copy of every receipt and stamped document for your records after closing, in case a title question comes up later.

sections.h2: Which route gets a Hoffman Estates house sold fastest?
sections.html:
Pick based on how much time and repair work you can take on.

  • Market the house openly. Exposure is greatest, though the sale then rides on the buyer's loan, appraisal and inspection.
  • Handle the sale yourself. You decide everything and also do the paperwork, stamp steps included.
  • Take a cash offer. Closing can be set to your date and the house is taken as is, which suits a tenant-occupied property or one with deferred repairs.

A cash sale has no lender appraisal or loan approval to wait on, so the Village steps above are usually the only clock running.

faqs.q: How many people live in Hoffman Estates?
faqs.a: The 2020 census found 52,530. The mid-2025 estimate is 50,858.

faqs.q: What does the Village transfer stamp cost?
faqs.a: The Village prints $3 per $1,000 of the selling price, and the seller pays. An exempt stamp has a $10.00 administrative fee.

faqs.q: Which county office files a Hoffman Estates deed?
faqs.a: Cook County for nearly every parcel. A very small part of the village is in Kane County, so check the parcel first.

faqs.q: How much lead time does the stamp need?
faqs.a: The Village asks for 48 hours of notice. Request the final water bill at 847-843-4824 at least five days before you buy the stamp.

faqs.q: Which district will my Hoffman Estates children attend?
faqs.a: That follows the street. In the north, east of Huntington Boulevard is CCSD 15 for grades K to 8 and west of it is Barrington 220, while addresses west of Barrington Road mostly go to Elgin Area U46.
